case_name: Priya Gupta v State Of Chhatishgarh & Ors
facts: The Department of Medical and Family Welfare, Government of Chhattisgarh, vide its letter dated 10th September, 2010 cancelled the admission granted to Akansha Adile and Priya Gupta in the MBBS course for the academic year 2006-07 in the Government NMDC Medical College, Jagdalpur.

The High Court, vide its judgment dated 9th August, 2011, held that admission to these petitioners had been given ignoring more meritorious and suitable candidates, which amounted to violation of natural justice to such other candidates and declined to interfere in the impugned order dated 10th September 2010.
The appellants had appeared in the Pre-Medical Test conducted by the State of Chhattisgarh for the academic year 2006.
48 students under different categories were given admission as per the list published by the Jagdalpur College on 30th September, 2006.

The Dean of the Jagdalpur College was further informed by the Committee, on 30th September, 2006 itself, that only two candidates, i.e., the appellants were available and they were given admission to the vacant seats.

Appellant No.2, Akansha Adile is stated to be daughter of the Director, Medical Education Government of Chhattisgarh, one Dr. S.L. Adile, who is supposed to be the highest authority in the State directly responsible for admission to the medical colleges, including Jagdalpur College.
A Right to Information application was filed before the Directorate General of Medical Services, Medical Examination Cell, New Delhi by one Dr. Anil Khakhariya.
issues: What is the validity of the admission granted to Akansha Adile and Priya Gupta in the MBBS course for the academic year 2006-07 in the Government NMDC Medical College, Jagdalpur?
Whether the admission was given ignoring more meritorious and suitable candidates, which amounted to violation of natural justice to such other candidates?
petitioner_arguments: The appellants had appeared in the Pre-Medical Test conducted by the State of Chhattisgarh for the academic year 2006.
The appellants were given admission and they joined the course of MBBS.
The admission was granted on the basis of merit and not based on any irregularity or malpractice.
respondent_arguments: The Department of Medical and Family Welfare, Government of Chhattisgarh, vide its letter dated 10th September, 2010 cancelled the admission granted to Akansha Adile and Priya Gupta in the MBBS course for the academic year 2006-07 in the Government NMDC Medical College, Jagdalpur.
The admission was given ignoring more meritorious and suitable candidates, which amounted to violation of natural justice to such other candidates.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the admission granted to Akansha Adile and Priya Gupta was valid and not violative of any rules or guidelines.
The Court observed that the appellants had appeared in the Pre-Medical Test conducted by the State of Chhattisgarh for the academic year 2006 and were given admission on the basis of merit.
The Court rejected the contention that the admission was given ignoring more meritorious and suitable candidates, which amounted to violation of natural justice to such other candidates.
holding: The Supreme Court allowed the appeals and set aside the order cancelling the admission granted to Akansha Adile and Priya Gupta in the MBBS course for the academic year 2006-07 in the Government NMDC Medical College, Jagdalpur.
The Court held that the admission was valid and not violative of any rules or guidelines.
